data_type_evidence: Paper states the experiments use ToxiGen and specifically the HuggingFace dataset `skg/toxigen-data` ([paper_claude-sonnet-4.6.md:118]).
The experiment folder contains an executable runner (`run_experiment.py`) plus supporting modules rather than only hardcoded result arrays ([run_experiment.py:74], [README.md:28]).
The main runner loads data through `load_toxigen_data(max_samples=DATASET_SIZE, seed=SEED)` before training and evaluation ([run_experiment.py:85-91]).

`data_processing.py` imports `load_dataset` from the Hugging Face `datasets` library and loads the real dataset `skg/toxigen-data` in `load_toxigen_data` ([data_processing.py:5], [data_processing.py:10-24]).
Configuration fixes real-dataset split sizes (`DATASET_SIZE = 2000`, `CALIBRATION_SIZE = 400`, `TEST_SIZE = 600`), consistent with a real benchmark evaluation setup ([config.py:11-13]).

No saved result artifacts (`results.json`, `experiment_results.json`, `log.txt`, `*.npy`, `*.csv`) were present in the inspected experiment folder at analysis time, so execution could not be independently verified from outputs alone.

Nuance: some downstream annotations/subsets are simulated heuristics (`assign_risk_categories`, `create_domain_test_sets`), but the primary experimental corpus is still a real benchmark dataset ([data_processing.py:153-169], [data_processing.py:195-219]).
